_readme: Knowledge scopes recognized by the RAG system (PLAN 10, ADR-0011). This is THE single canonical allowlist: it is the ONE place that decides which Confluence tag is a knowledge scope, and it is read by (a) the backend at startup, (b) the widget build, which generates its scope list directly from this file, and (c) Confluence ingestion eligibility (planned; see the ingestion substep). To recognize a new integration platform: add an entry below, then label the matching Confluence pages with that exact 'name' (case-insensitive — Confluence lowercases labels) — nothing else in the codebase needs to change. Every entry has three fields: 'name' (the exact Confluence tag and internal scope identifier), 'label' (the human-readable name the widget displays), and 'description' (what the scope contains). Startup validation (substep 1.2.1): every 'name' must be lowercase and unique, and both 'obi-general-test' and 'classified' must be present, or the backend exits non-zero. 'obi-general-test' is the always-included base scope; it is the scope untagged content falls into and is always allowed at retrieval. 'classified' is a RESERVED scope: it must be present here but is never a recognized/offerable scope — it is excluded from GET /health and from the widget's scope list, and a request can never select it (ADR-0011). platforms.json (not this file) still decides which recognized scopes each platform/integration may actually access.

scopes.name: obi-general-test
scopes.label: General
scopes.description: Base scope: content that applies to all customers/platforms. Always present, always allowed, never inferred from an untagged chunk (ADR-0011 Decision 1).

scopes.name: obi-toast-test
scopes.label: Toast
scopes.description: Toast POS integration content. Third-party platform — not this repo's own codename (see ADR-0011).

scopes.name: classified
scopes.label: Classified
scopes.description: Reserved scope. Must be present so the backend knows it, but is never offered by the widget, never listed by GET /health, and never selectable by a request body. A 'classified' Confluence label removes a page from the index (design rule #5).
